member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandPolicy
member.summary:
Pure command policy for run_commands (no AutoCAD references). Every step's command and every input is checked BEFORE anything is typed:
Blocked (never typed): SHELL/SH and the operating-system commands of acad.pgp, APPLOAD, NETLOAD, ARX, VBA*, ACTIVEX*, SCRIPT, VLISP, WEBLOAD, CUI/menu loading, QUIT, EXIT, CLOSE, CLOSEALL, OPEN, NEW, QNEW, RECOVER and other file-opening commands, UNDO/U (the copilot has its own undo tool), security system variables, dialog-only commands with no command-line version, and any command or input starting with "(" or "!" (AutoLISP).
Needs approval: SAVE, QSAVE, SAVEAS, WBLOCK, EXPORT*, PLOT, PUBLISH, PURGE, LAYDEL, LAYMRG, AUDIT, other file writers, and ERASE (or CUTCLIP) with the selection keyword ALL.
Names are normalised first (leading _ . - + and the transparent ' stripped, upper case) and aliases resolved (built-in default acad.pgp aliases plus the user's acad.pgp when given).

member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.DraftingPace
member.summary:
How fast the copilot types AutoCAD commands (process-wide, thread-safe).
Watch mode (the default) pauses between typed inputs () and before each new command () so the user can follow every command and number in the command line and see the objects appear one by one. Fast mode ( = false) types without pauses; AutoCAD still finishes each input before the next one is typed.
The panel binds its Watch/Fast switch to ; the drafting engine reads the delays before every pause, so a change applies to the very next input, also in the middle of a running call. is raised on the thread that changed the mode (any thread) after the new value is visible, and only when the value really changed; handlers that touch WPF must marshal to the dispatcher themselves.

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Tools.ToolDefinition.NamePattern
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,63}$
Options:
RegexOptions.CultureInvariant
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match a character in the set [a-z].
○ Match a character in the set [0-9_a-z] atomically at least 1 and at most 63 times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.
